sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktaḥ śakuninā rājā duryodhanas tadā dhṛtarāṣṭram idaṃ vākyam apadāntaram abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by Śakuni, King Duryodhana then spoke these words unhesitatingly to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: ayam utsahate rājañ śriyam āhartum akṣavit dyūtena pāṇḍuputrasya tad anujñātum arhasi
english: "This one, O king, is skilled at dice and is eager to win the wealth of the son of Pāṇḍu by gambling — you ought to give your permission for this."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kṣattā mantrī mahāprājñaḥ sthito yasyāsmi śāsane tena saṃgamya vetsyāmi kāryasyāsya viniścayam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Vidura is the counsellor of great wisdom, by whose guidance I abide. Having consulted with him, I shall determine what is to be done in this matter."

sanskrit: sa hi dharmaṃ puraskṛtya dīrghadarśī paraṃ hitam ubhayoḥ pakṣayor yuktaṃ vakṣyaty arthaviniścayam
english: "For he, placing dharma foremost, far-sighted as he is, will declare what is supremely beneficial and what is proper for both sides, and will settle the matter definitively."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca nivartayiṣyati tvāsau yadi kṣattā sameṣyati nivṛtte tvayi rājendra mariṣye 'ham asaṃśayam
english: Duryodhana said: "If Vidura comes and dissuades you, then if you too desist, O king of kings, I shall surely die — there is no doubt of this."

sanskrit: sa mayi tvaṃ mṛte rājan vidureṇa sukhī bhava bhokṣyase pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ kiṃ mayā tvaṃ kariṣyasi
english: "When I am dead, O king, be happy with Vidura — you will enjoy the whole earth; what use will you have of me?"

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ārtavākyaṃ tu tat tasya praṇayoktaṃ niśamya saḥ dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bravīt preṣyān duryodhanamate sthitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing that anguished and affectionate speech of his, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, yielding to Duryodhana's will, spoke to his servants.

sanskrit: sthūṇāsahasrair bṛhatīṃ śatadvārāṃ sabhāṃ mama manoramāṃ darśanīyām āśu kurvantu śilpinaḥ
english: "Let craftsmen quickly build for me a great and beautiful assembly hall with a thousand pillars and a hundred doors, pleasing to the mind and fair to behold."

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃstīrya ratnais tām akṣān āvāpya sarvaśaḥ sukṛtāṃ supraveśāṃ ca nivedayata me śanaiḥ
english: "Then, having spread it with jewels and provided dice in every place, and when it is well finished and easily accessible, report to me gently."

sanskrit: duryodhanasya śāntyartham iti niścitya bhūmipaḥ dhṛtarāṣṭro mahārāja prāhiṇod vidurāya vai
english: Having thus resolved for the sake of pacifying Duryodhana, O great king, Dhṛtarāṣṭra then sent a messenger to Vidura.

sanskrit: apṛṣṭvā viduraṃ hy asya nāsīt kaś cid viniścayaḥ dyūtadoṣāṃś ca jānan sa putrasnehād akṛṣyata
english: For without consulting Vidura he could reach no firm resolution on anything; yet knowing the vices of gambling, he was drawn along by his love for his son.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā viduro dhīmān kalidvāram upasthitam vināśamukham utpannaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭram upādravat
english: Hearing this, the wise Vidura, seeing that the gateway of Kali had arrived and that destruction's mouth had opened, hastened to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamya mahātmānaṃ bhrātā bhrātaram agrajam mūrdhnā praṇamya caraṇāv idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Approaching that great-souled elder brother, brother to brother, and bowing his head at his feet, he spoke these words.

sanskrit: nābhinandāmi te rājan vyavasāyam imaṃ prabho putrair bhedo yathā na syād dyūtahetos tathā kuru
english: "I do not rejoice in this resolve of yours, O king, O lord. Act in such a way that there may be no quarrel among your sons on account of gambling."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kṣattaḥ putreṣu putrair me kalaho na bhaviṣyati divi devāḥ prasādaṃ naḥ kariṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: "Vidura, no quarrel will come among my sons through their sons; the gods in heaven will surely grant us their grace — there is no doubt."

sanskrit: aśubhaṃ vā śubhaṃ vāpi hitaṃ vā yadi vāhitam pravartatāṃ suhṛddyūtaṃ diṣṭam etan na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Whether auspicious or inauspicious, beneficial or harmful, let this friendly gambling proceed — this is fate, without a doubt."

sanskrit: mayi saṃnihite caiva bhīṣme ca bharatarṣabhe anayo daivavihito na kathaṃ cid bhaviṣyati
english: "With me present, and with Bhīṣma, that bull among Bhāratas, any mischief decreed by fate will not come to pass in any manner."

sanskrit: gaccha tvaṃ ratham āsthāya hayair vātasamair jave khāṇḍavaprastham adyaiva samānaya yudhiṣṭhiram
english: "Go, mounting a chariot with horses swift as the wind, and bring Yudhiṣṭhira from Khāṇḍavaprastha today itself."

sanskrit: na vāryo vyavasāyo me viduraitad bravīmi te daivam eva paraṃ manye yenaitad upapadyate
english: "My resolve cannot be checked — I tell you this, Vidura. I hold fate alone to be supreme, by which this comes to pass."

sanskrit: ity ukto viduro dhīmān naitad astīti cintayan āpageyaṃ mahāprājñam abhyagacchat suduḥkhitaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the wise Vidura, thinking "this must not be," went deeply grieved to the great-minded Bhīṣma, son of the river goddess.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca kathaṃ samabhavad dyūtaṃ bhrātṝṇāṃ tan mahātyayam yatra tad vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ pāṇḍavair me pitāmahaiḥ
english: Janamejaya said: "How did that gambling among the brothers come to be — that great calamity wherein my grandfathers the Pāṇḍavas met that disaster?"

sanskrit: ke ca tatra sabhāstārā rājāno brahmavittama ke cainam anvamodanta ke cainaṃ pratyaṣedhayan
english: "Who were the kings assembled there, O best of knowers of the Veda? Who approved of it and who tried to prevent it?"

sanskrit: vistareṇaitad icchāmi kathyamānaṃ tvayā dvija mūlaṃ hy etad vināśasya pṛthivyā dvijasattama
english: "I wish to hear this told in detail by you, O twice-born one, for this is the root of the destruction of the earth, O best of twice-born men."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam uktas tadā rājñā vyāsaśiṣyaḥ pratāpavān ācacakṣe yathāvṛttaṃ tat sarvaṃ sarvavedavit
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed by the king, the illustrious disciple of Vyāsa, the knower of all the Vedas, narrated everything as it had occurred.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇu me vistareṇemāṃ kathāṃ bharatasattama bhūya eva mahārāja yadi te śravaṇe matiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: "Hear from me this story in detail, O best of Bhāratas — again, O great king, if your mind is inclined to hear it."

sanskrit: vidurasya mataṃ jñātvā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'mbikāsutaḥ duryodhanam idaṃ vākyam uvāca vijane punaḥ
english: Having learned Vidura's opinion, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Ambikā, once again spoke these words to Duryodhana in private.

sanskrit: alaṃ dyūtena gāndhāre viduro na praśaṃsati na hy asau sumahābuddhir ahitaṃ no vadiṣyati
english: "Enough of gambling, O son of Gāndhārī — Vidura does not approve. For that one of great wisdom will not speak what is harmful to us."

sanskrit: hitaṃ hi paramaṃ manye viduro yat prabhāṣate kriyatāṃ putra tat sarvam etan manye hitaṃ tava
english: "I hold whatever Vidura speaks to be supremely beneficial; let all of that be done, my son — I consider this to be your good."

sanskrit: devarṣir vāsavagurur devarājāya dhīmate yat prāha śāstraṃ bhagavān bṛhaspatir udāradhīḥ
english: "The divine sage Bṛhaspati, of noble mind, the teacher of Vāsava, taught the holy wisdom to the wise king of gods —"

sanskrit: tad veda viduraḥ sarvaṃ sarahasyaṃ mahākaviḥ sthitaś ca vacane tasya sadāham api putraka
english: "— all of that with its secrets does Vidura know, that great sage; and I too, my son, am ever abiding in his words."

sanskrit: viduro vāpi medhāvī kurūṇāṃ pravaro mataḥ uddhavo vā mahābuddhir vṛṣṇīnām arcito nṛpa
english: "Indeed, the intelligent Vidura is considered the foremost among the Kurus, as Uddhava of great wisdom is honoured among the Vṛṣṇis, O prince."

sanskrit: dyūtena tad alaṃ putra dyūte bhedo hi dṛśyate bhede vināśo rājyasya tat putra parivarjaya
english: "Therefore enough of gambling, my son — in gambling, division is clearly seen; in division, destruction of the kingdom follows. Avoid it, son."

sanskrit: pitrā mātrā ca putrasya yad vai kāryaṃ paraṃ smṛtam prāptas tvam asi tat tāta pitṛpaitāmahaṃ padam
english: "What is remembered as the highest duty of a father and mother toward their son — that position of your fathers and grandfathers you have already attained, dear child."

sanskrit: adhītavān kṛtī śāstre lālitaṃ satataṃ gṛhe bhrātṛjyeṣṭhaḥ sthito rājye vindase kiṃ na śobhanam
english: "You are learned, accomplished in the scriptures, cherished always at home, the eldest brother established in the kingdom — what beautiful thing do you lack?"

sanskrit: pṛthagjanair alabhyaṃ yad bhojanācchādanaṃ param tat prāpto 'si mahābāho kasmāc chocasi putraka
english: "What food and clothing of the highest order, unattainable by ordinary men, that you have obtained, O mighty-armed — why then do you grieve, my son?"

sanskrit: sphītaṃ rāṣṭraṃ mahābāho pitṛpaitāmahaṃ mahat nityam ājñāpayan bhāsi divi deveśvaro yathā
english: "O mighty-armed, commanding the great and flourishing kingdom of your fathers and grandfathers constantly, you shine like the lord of gods in heaven."

sanskrit: tasya te viditaprajña śokamūlam idaṃ katham samutthitaṃ duḥkhataraṃ tan me śaṃsitum arhasi
english: "For you, O one of discerning wisdom, how has this most painful root of sorrow arisen? You ought to tell me that."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca aśnāmy ācchādayāmīti prapaśyan pāpapūruṣaḥ nāmarṣaṃ kurute yas tu puruṣaḥ so 'dhamaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: Duryodhana said: "'I eat, I am clothed' — a man who, seeing these things, feels no indignation is considered a base person."

sanskrit: na māṃ prīṇāti rājendra lakṣmīḥ sādhāraṇā vibho jvalitām iva kaunteye śriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca vivyathe
english: "Shared prosperity does not delight me, O king of kings, O lord; and having seen the blazing glory of the son of Kuntī, I am pierced with anguish."

sanskrit: sarvāṃ hi pṛthivīṃ dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiravaśānugām sthiro 'smi yo 'haṃ jīvāmi duḥkhād etad bravīmi te
english: "That I remain steadfast after seeing all the earth subject to Yudhiṣṭhira's command — I tell you this out of grief: that is why I live."

sanskrit: āvarjitā ivābhānti nighnāś caitrakikaukurāḥ kāraskarā lohajaṅghā yudhiṣṭhiraniveśane
english: "The Chaitrakikas, the Kukuras, the Karaskaras, the Lohajanghas — they shine there as though enchanted and subdued, at Yudhiṣṭhira's dwelling."

sanskrit: himavatsāgarānūpāḥ sarvaratnākarās tathā antyāḥ sarve paryudastā yudhiṣṭhiraniveśane
english: "Those who dwell along the Himālayas and the sea, all the treasuries of jewels, even the outcastes — all have been subdued and stand suppliant at Yudhiṣṭhira's dwelling."

sanskrit: jyeṣṭho 'yam iti māṃ matvā śreṣṭhaś ceti viśāṃ pate yudhiṣṭhireṇa satkṛtya yukto ratnaparigrahe
english: "Thinking me the eldest and the most worthy, O lord of the people, I was honored by Yudhiṣṭhira and appointed to receive the jewels."

sanskrit: upasthitānāṃ ratnānāṃ śreṣṭhānām arghahāriṇām nādṛśyata paraḥ prānto nāparas tatra bhārata
english: "Of the finest jewels being presented, those of the highest worth, no farther end could be seen — no other boundary either — O Bhārata."

sanskrit: na me hastaḥ samabhavad vasu tat pratigṛhṇataḥ prātiṣṭhanta mayi śrānte gṛhya dūrāhṛtaṃ vasu
english: "My hand was not equal to receiving all that wealth; as I grew tired, others took and accepted the wealth brought from distant lands."

sanskrit: kṛtāṃ bindusaroratnair mayena sphāṭikacchadām apaśyaṃ nalinīṃ pūrṇām udakasyeva bhārata
english: "I saw a lotus pool built by Maya with the jewels of lake Bindu, its floor of crystal, full as if it were water, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: vastram utkarṣati mayi prāhasat sa vṛkodaraḥ śatror ṛddhiviśeṣeṇa vimūḍhaṃ ratnavarjitam
english: "As my garments were lifted up, that wolf-bellied one — Bhīma — laughed at me, confused and stripped of jewels by the exceptional prosperity of the enemy."

sanskrit: tatra sma yadi śaktaḥ syāṃ pātayeyaṃ vṛkodaram sapatnenāvahāso hi sa māṃ dahati bhārata
english: "Had I been able to do so there, I would have felled that wolf-belly — for the mockery of an enemy burns me, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: punaś ca tādṛśīm eva vāpīṃ jalajaśālinīm matvā śilāsamāṃ toye patito 'smi narādhipa
english: "And again, mistaking a similar pool adorned with water-born flowers for solid ground, I fell into the water, O lord of men."

sanskrit: tatra māṃ prāhasat kṛṣṇaḥ pārthena saha sasvanam draupadī ca saha strībhir vyathayantī mano mama
english: "There Kṛṣṇa laughed at me with a ringing sound, together with Pārtha; and Draupadī too, along with her women, tormenting my heart."

sanskrit: klinnavastrasya ca jale kiṃkarā rājacoditāḥ dadur vāsāṃsi me 'nyāni tac ca duḥkhataraṃ mama
english: "And while I stood wet in the water, the servants, directed by the king, gave me different garments — and that too was most painful to me."

sanskrit: pralambhaṃ ca śṛṇuṣvānyaṃ gadato me narādhipa advāreṇa vinirgacchan dvārasaṃsthānarūpiṇā abhihatya śilāṃ bhūyo lalāṭenāsmi vikṣataḥ
english: "Hear yet another humiliation I tell you, O lord of men: going out through what was no door but was shaped like a door, I struck the stone and was wounded again on my forehead."

sanskrit: tatra māṃ yamajau dūrād ālokya lalitau kila bāhubhiḥ parigṛhṇītāṃ śocantau sahitāv ubhau
english: "There the twin brothers, seeing me from afar, graceful as they were, both embraced me with their arms, sorrowful together, so they said."

sanskrit: uvāca sahadevas tu tatra māṃ vismayann iva idaṃ dvāram ito gaccha rājann iti punaḥ punaḥ
english: "And Sahadeva, as if marveling, said to me there, 'Go this way, O king, this is the door' — saying it again and again."

sanskrit: nāmadheyāni ratnānāṃ purastān na śrutāni me yāni dṛṣṭāni me tasyāṃ manas tapati tac ca me
english: "The names of the jewels that I saw there had never been heard by me before — and that too torments my mind."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca yan mayā pāṇḍavānāṃ tu dṛṣṭaṃ tac chṛṇu bhārata āhṛtaṃ bhūmipālair hi vasu mukhyaṃ tatas tataḥ
english: Duryodhana said: "Hear what I saw at the Pāṇḍavas' court, O Bhārata — the finest wealth brought by kings from here and there."

sanskrit: na vinde dṛḍham ātmānaṃ dṛṣṭvāhaṃ tad arer dhanam phalato bhūmito vāpi pratipadyasva bhārata
english: "I cannot find firmness in myself having seen that wealth of the enemy — understand this from its fruits and from the ground reality, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: aiḍāṃś cailān vārṣadaṃśāñ jātarūpapariṣkṛtān prāvārājinamukhyāṃś ca kāmbojaḥ pradadau vasu
english: "The Kāmboja king gave wealth of the finest kind: garments of the Aila and Vaila and Varsha-damsha peoples adorned with gold, cloaks and skins of the highest quality."

sanskrit: aśvāṃs tittirikalmāṣāṃs triśataṃ śukanāsikān uṣṭravāmīs triśataṃ ca puṣṭāḥ pīluśamīṅgudaiḥ
english: "Three hundred horses of the Tittiri and Kalmasha breeds with parrot-like noses, and three hundred she-camels fattened on pilu, shami, and ingudi trees."

sanskrit: govāsanā brāhmaṇāś ca dāsamīyāś ca sarvaśaḥ prītyarthaṃ te mahābhāgā dharmarājño mahātmanaḥ trikharvaṃ balim ādāya dvāri tiṣṭhanti vāritāḥ
english: "Brahmin ascetics with cow-leather garments and servant-attendants of every kind, those greatly blessed ones, stood at the door waiting, bearing three kharva loads of tribute out of affection for the great-souled king of righteousness."

sanskrit: kamaṇḍalūn upādāya jātarūpamayāñ śubhān evaṃ baliṃ pradāyātha praveśaṃ lebhire tataḥ
english: "Having brought water-pots made of pure gold, auspicious ones, and having thus presented their tribute, they then gained entry."

sanskrit: śataṃ dāsīsahasrāṇāṃ kārpāsikanivāsinām śyāmās tanvyo dīrghakeśyo hemābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ śūdrā viprottamārhāṇi rāṅkavāny ajināni ca
english: "One hundred thousand maidservants from the Karpasika lands — dark, slender, long-haired, adorned with golden ornaments — along with Śūdras worthy of the finest brahmins, with wool-cloths and skins."

sanskrit: baliṃ ca kṛtsnam ādāya bharukacchanivāsinaḥ upaninyur mahārāja hayān gāndhāradeśajān
english: "The inhabitants of Bharukaccha, bearing their full tribute, brought, O great king, horses bred in the Gāndhāra country."

sanskrit: indrakṛṣṭair vartayanti dhānyair nadīmukhaiś ca ye samudraniṣkuṭe jātāḥ parisindhu ca mānavāḥ
english: "Those men who live by grain sown by Indra's grace, at the mouths of rivers and in the island-forests of the ocean, and along the Sindhu —"

sanskrit: te vairāmāḥ pāradāś ca vaṅgāś ca kitavaiḥ saha vividhaṃ balim ādāya ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: "— those Vairajas, the Paradasas and the Vaṅgas, together with gamesters, bringing varied tribute and diverse jewels —"

sanskrit: ajāvikaṃ gohiraṇyaṃ kharoṣṭraṃ phalajaṃ madhu kambalān vividhāṃś caiva dvāri tiṣṭhanti vāritāḥ
english: "— goats and sheep, cattle and gold, donkeys and camels, fruit-produced honey, and various woolen blankets, stood waiting at the door, held back."

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣādhipaḥ śūro mlecchānām adhipo balī yanavaiḥ sahito rājā bhagadatto mahārathaḥ
english: "Bhagadatta, the heroic lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, the powerful overlord of the Mlecchas, the great warrior-king, came together with the Yavanas —"

sanskrit: ājāneyān hayāñ śīghrān ādāyānilaraṃhasaḥ baliṃ ca kṛtsnam ādāya dvāri tiṣṭhati vāritaḥ
english: "— bringing swift thoroughbred horses with the speed of wind, and bearing his full tribute, stood at the door, waiting."

sanskrit: aśmasāramayaṃ bhāṇḍaṃ śuddhadantatsarūn asīn prāgjyotiṣo 'tha tad dattvā bhagadatto 'vrajat tadā
english: "Bhagadatta of Prāgjyotiṣa, having given that vessel made of the finest iron-ore, and swords with handles of pure ivory, then departed."

sanskrit: dvyakṣāṃs tryakṣāṃl lalāṭākṣān nānādigbhyaḥ samāgatān auṣṇīṣān anivāsāṃś ca bāhukān puruṣādakān
english: "Two-eyed and three-eyed men, those with an eye in the forehead, assembled from various directions, those wearing turbans and those dwelling without fixed abode, the Bahukas and the man-eaters —"

sanskrit: ekapādāṃś ca tatrāham apaśyaṃ dvāri vāritān balyarthaṃ dadatas tasmai hiraṇyaṃ rajataṃ bahu
english: "— and one-footed beings I saw there, waiting at the door, giving him much gold and silver as tribute."

sanskrit: indragopakavarṇābhāñ śukavarṇān manojavān tathaivendrāyudhanibhān saṃdhyābhrasadṛśān api
english: "Horses of the color of the Indragopaka insect, of parrot-green color and swift as thought, others resembling Indra's rainbow, and some like twilight clouds —"

sanskrit: anekavarṇān āraṇyān gṛhītvāśvān manojavān jātarūpam anarghyaṃ ca dadus tasyaikapādakāḥ
english: "— the one-footed beings took those many-colored forest horses of mind-like speed and gave him gold beyond all price."

sanskrit: cīnān hūṇāñ śakān oḍrān parvatāntaravāsinaḥ vārṣṇeyān hārahūṇāṃś ca kṛṣṇān haimavatāṃs tathā
english: "The Chinas, the Hunas, the Śakas, the Oḍras, dwellers in mountain fastnesses, the Vārṣṇeyas, the Harahunas, the dark ones, and those of the Himavat region —"

sanskrit: na pārayāmy abhigatān vividhān dvāri vāritān balyarthaṃ dadatas tasya nānārūpān anekaśaḥ
english: "— I cannot enumerate all those who came in their various forms, waiting at the door, giving him tribute of many kinds in countless numbers."

sanskrit: kṛṣṇagrīvān mahākāyān rāsabhāñ śatapātinaḥ āhārṣur daśasāhasrān vinītān dikṣu viśrutān
english: "They brought ten thousand black-necked, huge-bodied asses, capable of a hundred leagues, tame and celebrated in all directions."

sanskrit: pramāṇarāgasparśāḍhyaṃ bāhlīcīnasamudbhavam aurṇaṃ ca rāṅkavaṃ caiva kīṭajaṃ paṭṭajaṃ tathā
english: "Woolen cloth and Rankava cloth, insect-produced silk and woven silk, rich in measure, color, and texture, produced in Bahlika and China —"

sanskrit: kuṭṭīkṛtaṃ tathaivānyat kamalābhaṃ sahasraśaḥ ślakṣṇaṃ vastram akārpāsam āvikaṃ mṛdu cājinam
english: "— beaten cloth and other fabrics of lotus-like appearance in thousands, smooth non-cotton cloth, soft sheep-wool cloth, and deer-skins —"

sanskrit: niśitāṃś caiva dīrghāsīn ṛṣṭiśaktiparaśvadhān aparāntasamudbhūtāṃs tathaiva paraśūñ śitān
english: "— sharpened and long swords, lances, spears, and battle-axes, and also sharp axes produced in the western border lands —"

sanskrit: rasān gandhāṃś ca vividhān ratnāni ca sahasraśaḥ baliṃ ca kṛtsnam ādāya dvāri tiṣṭhanti vāritāḥ
english: "— various juices and fragrances, and jewels by the thousands — bearing all this tribute in full, they stood waiting at the door."
